subject: Post-call alignment: VPC constraints, data residency, and next decisions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anil Rao <anil.rao@medivita.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@medivita.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call alignment: VPC constraints, data residency, and next decisions

Thanks for the time this morning — good conversation. Short recap below and a proposed next set of actions so we can keep momentum on the pilot procurement. Please reply with clarifications where needed.

Key pain points you shared
- Must keep PHI inside US (primary region us-east-1) and no cross-region backups without explicit controls.
- Procurement wants an air-gap-capable path (comfortable with an isolated VPC peering model or an on-prem appliance).
- Strict egress controls: only specific outbound IPs allowed, and no direct internet access from compute nodes.
- SIEM/Log forwarding requirement: Splunk or Sumo compatible with TLS mutual auth.

Goals we agreed on
- Technical deep-dive week of Jul 12 to validate network design and egress model.
- Proof-of-concept (3-month pilot) running on a private VPC with KMS-managed keys and explicit audit logs.
- Procurement to review SOW draft for pilot budget approval by Jul 23.

Open questions / blockers
- Can Medivita allow our small set of egress IPs and an outbound NAT with strict ACLs? (Anil — need confirmation from infra team).
- Do you require an on-prem air-gap appliance for initial pilot or would a VPC-only approach be acceptable for pilot scope?
- KMS/HSM constraints: will you accept Redwood-managed CMKs under a dedicated key policy, or must keys be in your customer-managed KMS?

Attachments included: network-diagram-v1.png (annotated), redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx, and an initial SOW draft (mvp-sow-draft.pdf).

Proposed next steps (please pick or add)
1) Anil / Priya: confirm egress/IP allowlist window and KMS preference by Thu Jul 8.
2) Redwood: schedule technical deep-dive (1.5 hrs) with infra + networking — propose Tue Jul 13 10:00–11:30 PT.
3) Jordan/Monica: prepare detailed checklist and preflight questions for the deep-dive.
4) Procurement: we will share a stripped SOW for pilot and cost bands within 48 hours.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 415-555-0123

From: Anil Rao <anil.rao@medivita.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@medivita.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call alignment: VPC constraints, data residency, and next decisions

Rachel — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from infra:
- We can allow an outbound NAT to a small set of IPs but need a CIDR range (we prefer /28 or larger). We will check whether an explicit allowlist of third-party IPs is acceptable vs requiring a VPC endpoint.
- Backups: any managed snapshot service must remain in us-east-1; cross-region replication requires a signed exception.
- KMS: for the pilot we prefer customer-managed keys (we run AWS KMS in our account). If Redwood can demonstrate key access patterns and a key policy, we can proceed.

One ask: can you include the port ranges and protocol for SIEM forwarding? Our security team will require specifics before the deep-dive.

I can confirm answers on egress and CIDR by Thu Jul 8. Also, Jul 13 at 10:00 PT works for the team.

—Anil
Anil Rao
VP, Infrastructure | Medivita Health
anil.rao@medivita.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anil Rao <anil.rao@medivita.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@medivita.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call alignment: VPC constraints, data residency, and next decisions

Thanks Anil — helpful. A few quick replies inline to make prep easier:
- CIDR/IPs: we will provide a short list of recommended egress /28 ranges and an alternate VPC endpoint design. See attached redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx -> tab 'IP Design'.
- Backups: confirmed — our recommended pilot uses in-region snapshots only. We will mark replication off by default in the POC config.
- KMS: we support customer-managed CMKs in your AWS account; Jordan will follow up with the exact policy template.
- SIEM forwarding: typical outbound is TCP 6514 (syslog over TLS); we also support HTTPS-based forwarding to Splunk HEC on 8088. Full port/protocol matrix attached.

I queued the technical deep-dive for Tue Jul 13 10:00–11:30 PT (invite to follow). For the deep-dive we'll bring the runtime engineer and networking lead (Jordan and Monica) and a short live preview of the private VPC routing.

Next actions for you: confirm egress/CIDR by Thu Jul 8. If you prefer an HSM-only key approach, flag that ASAP so we can scope accordingly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Rachel

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Medivita pre-call prep and owner list (internal only)

Internal notes (do not forward) — summary of what to bring to the Jul 13 deep-dive:
- Jordan: bring sample IAM role trust policy and the CMK policy template we use for customer-kept keys. Ensure we have an example CloudWatch/Syslog forwarding config.
- Monica: prepare the network diagram with two variants (VPC-peering NAT vs. VPC endpoint + private link). Mark which requires any infra changes on Redwood side. Attach updated network-diagram-v1.png (I updated the peering lane labels).
- Lauren: I need a prioritized ask list for procurement (pilot SOW change notes, pricing bands, and a redline-friendly SOW). Draft in the attached mvp-sow-draft.pdf — add comments by EOD Jul 9 so we can share a clean version with Medivita on Jul 10.

Risks to call out:
- If Medivita requires in-account HSM only (no CMK sharing), timeline for pilot expands — flag as potential blocker.
- Egress allowlist negotiations can push procurement if security requires more approvals.

I'll consolidate final slide notes after the Medivita confirmations on Thu.

Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
summary: Post-call sales thread summarizing Medivita requirements for a private VPC/on-prem pilot (data residency, egress allowlist, KMS preferences). Includes attachments and clear next steps: confirm CIDR by Jul 8, technical deep-dive scheduled Jul 13, procurement SOW milestone Jul 23.
